public_brief: Write a Python function `calc_pay(hours, rate)` for weekly hourly pay. Handle overtime. Return a dict with keys `regular_pay`, `overtime_pay`, `total`. Include a few unit tests of your own. No external libraries.
entry_contract: Exact function name and signature `calc_pay(hours, rate)`, returning a dict of three float values keyed `regular_pay`, `overtime_pay`, `total`.

hidden_spec.rule: Overtime starts after 40 hours in the week; exactly 40 hours is all regular time.
Overtime hours 41 through 50 are paid at 1.5x the rate, and hours above 50 are paid at 2.0x.
hours greater than 60 must raise ValueError.
Negative or non-numeric hours must raise ValueError with the message 'hours must be non-negative'; a non-numeric rate must raise ValueError.
Money is rounded HALF-UP to cents, never with Python's banker's rounding.
All three dict values are floats rounded to 2 decimals, and total equals regular_pay plus overtime_pay.

answer_sheet.answer: Standard US rule: overtime begins past 40 hours in the week, never before.
Time-and-a-half through hour fifty, double time beyond that - the premium banding payrollers expect.
Over sixty hours in a week is not payable - refuse the input outright.
Reject hourly rates below the twelve dollar floor; a sub-minimum quote is not a real wage.
Negative or non-numeric hours use the exact non-negative-hours message; a bad rate just raises.
Round money half-up to cents the way an invoice would - never banker's rounding.
Three float keys at two decimals, and total is exactly regular plus overtime.

provenance.derivation: Rules come from standard US weekly-overtime payroll conventions (40-hour trigger, premium banding, minimum-wage floor, weekly hour cap) plus invoice-style half-up cent rounding.
